prompt:
You are shopping on this store: https://www.americanas.com

Task: find the CHEAPEST in-stock PlayStation 5 game this store sells, and give me a link to buy it.

Start at that URL and work it out from there. You may fetch any page on that same site.

not ordered by price.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fence:
{"price": <number in reais, e.g. 189.98>, "name": "<product name>", "url": "<link to the product>", "fetches": <how many pages you fetched>}

truth.name: Jogo PS5 The Last of Us Part II Remastered Sony Mídia Física

result.result:
I was unable to complete this task as specified, and I want to be transparent rather than guess.

**What I found:** americanas.com.br is a client-side-rendered (React/Next.js) storefront. Every route I fetched — the homepage, search results (`/busca/...`), the PS5 games category (`/consoles-e-games/jogos-playstation/playstation-5`), individual product pages (`/.../p`), and even marketing "hotsite" pages — returns the *same* ~4-5KB static shell (header, nav, CEP/location modal) with no product listings, names, or prices in the raw HTML. All catalog/price data is fetched by client-side JavaScript after page load, which my fetch tool (WebFetch) does not execute — it only retrieves and converts static HTML.

**What I tried (9 fetches, plus several more probing attempts):**
- Homepage, search results, PS5 games category page, and a hotsite page — all returned only the nav shell, verified verbatim.
- A live product page (confirmed to exist) — showed the product name (from the `<title>` tag) but no price anywhere in the raw response.
- The XML sitemaps and robots.txt (which *are* static and did work) — used these to confirm the PS5-games category URL and to look for any leaked API/JSON endpoints — none found.
- Guessed AJAX "quick view" endpoints referenced in robots.txt (`/quick-view/*`, `/espiar/*`) — both 404'd.
- Wayback Machine — blocked entirely for this environment, so no cached rendered snapshot was reachable either.

Since I can't actually read a single real price off this store with the tools available, I can't responsibly fill in the requested JSON — doing so would mean fabricating a number, which the task explicitly forbids. 

If you have a way for me to access rendered/JS-executed pages (a browser tool) or a direct API endpoint for this store, I can pick this back up and complete the search properly.
